issue: #576 — Flat reversion P5, family rebind lane B, reference-input-no-idx (Q31), on spec #565
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §5.3, §7.1, §8.8, §10.5 — field 1 reference inputs read through the §8.8 door by arithmetic at field 0's shared 38-byte stride, under authenticate-once
note:
Lane B's rolling re-measurement, attached as this lane's exit criterion per #565's measurement-slotting rule (AC3). The Q31 rebind swaps the counted `field_commitment_from_items` re-hash of a prover-reproduced item list for a single authenticate-once hash plus an O(1) arithmetic read (field 1, step-02) and an authenticated item-count read (field 2, step-04). It introduces NO new unbounded walk: step-02 is fixed-stride arithmetic and step-04 reads the §5.1 authenticated count, so there is no `basisFit:"exceeds"` row and no infeasibility string. Q31's cardinality-growth bound is the parent-owned Q1x envelope (`native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json`): field 1 shares field 0's 38-byte stride, so that ledger's field-0/1 stride rows and step-04 outputs-count rows apply unchanged. Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-q31-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. Provisional: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — structural failures (a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement by exceeding the basis) fail in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten.

**#584 re-take.** Both rows here rose by the same fixed **per-opening** amount, **+7,117 mem / +2,529,845 cpu**, when #584 gave `field_opening_v1` a multi-field opening: the single-field `opened_field_view`/`opened_field_walk` are now `anchored_native_tx` followed by `anchored_field_view`/`anchored_field_walk`, so a one-field step pays one extra opaque-record construction, the field reads that go with it, plus the two separate `expect`s `field_pairs_with` now spends so that a refusal names which guard fired. One amount covers both rows because both open a **body** field (`BodyTxOpening`, fields 1 and 2); it is the same figure the body half of `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json` records, where the witness-set half shows the second, larger amount. The shift being identical across the two rows is what makes it per-opening rather than per-item: it moves no growth figure and no `basisFit`, and it is under 0.06% of the §3.3 memory basis. The alternative was a second spelling of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor` and the §2.5 body/witness pairing for the single-field path, which the AGENTS.md tradeoff order (correctness, safety, liveness, performance) does not buy at that price.

**#586 re-take.** Step-02's row rose by **+1,312 mem / +358,482 cpu**; step-04's did not move. #586 gave `decode_midgard_tx_input_cbor` (`lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx/components.ak`) an exact-38-byte width guard — `expect bytearray.length(input_cbor) == midgard_tx_input_item_bytes` — because `decode_definite_bytes_at` would otherwise accept the non-minimal `59 0020` byte-string header and let a 39-byte item decode to the same out-ref as the canonical 38-byte one, giving one input two ledger-trie keys. The increase is that single length equality, charged **per execution that decodes an out-ref rather than per item**: step-02 does one §5.3 positional read of field 1 and pays it once, while step-04 reads the §5.1 authenticated output count and decodes no input at all. The same figure appears in `native-tx-q21-exec-ledger-v1.json`'s L2 row and in the Q10/Q11 rows of `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json` at 1 and at 296 spend inputs alike — identical at both cardinalities, which is what makes it per-execution. It moves no growth figure and no `basisFit`, and is under 0.01% of the §3.3 memory basis.

**#592 round-4 re-take, §8.3 erratum E1's repair of `K` (15,900 → 15,148).** Both rows here open the §8.8 door once, each on a **body** field, and both rose by **+2,224 mem / +682,801 cpu**. `chunk_bytes_k` is compiled into `native_tx_field_access_v1` and every door opening pays its `expected_chunk_count` / chunk-offset arithmetic, so this is a compiler-constant movement rather than a change in the step. That amount is what these two body-field rows measure and is not put forward as a universal per-opening constant: the same re-take moves the witness-field rows of `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json` by a smaller amount (+2,124 / +666,801), and the two-body-field L2 row of `native-tx-q21-exec-ledger-v1.json` by +4,248 / +1,333,602, which is twice that witness figure rather than twice this one. No judgement in this ledger moves: step-02 is still fixed-stride arithmetic, step-04 still reads the authenticated count, and there is still no `basisFit:"exceeds"` row.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair.** Bisected against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits rather than assumed: the pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` leaves every row below identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit, so the whole of the movement is the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — constant certificate asset name, mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality of that `field_hash` against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`. Both rows open the §8.8 door once on a body field, and — unlike every earlier re-take of this ledger — they moved by **different amounts and in opposite directions**: step-02 fell by **1,767 mem / 642,914 cpu** (1,860,355 → 1,858,588 and 781,797,639 → 781,154,725) while step-04 rose by **7,633 mem / 861,086 cpu** (1,841,619 → 1,849,252 and 778,626,324 → 779,487,410). That is stated rather than smoothed, and **no per-opening figure is published for this re-take**: `d528e00b` both deleted a per-field guard (`carriage_reaches_the_anchor`) and added a door equality on the certificate's mint-welded `field_hash`, and two readings that disagree in sign cannot separate them. The earlier per-opening constants this note publishes for #584, #586 and #592 are untouched, being readings of their own re-takes. No judgement in this ledger moves: step-02 is still fixed-stride arithmetic, step-04 still reads the §5.1 authenticated count, there is still no `basisFit:"exceeds"` row, and the parent-owned Q1x cardinality envelope still applies unchanged.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24. The report that the cap is unchanged at epoch 648 is corroboration only — no protocol-params artifact in this repository pins epoch 648.

compiler: Readings re-taken under the canonical patched fork `aiken v1.1.23+5adf783` (repo https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/aiken, tag `midgard-5adf7837`, rev 5adf7837cbddb5d329fd51d9c0cd73f561eaf95c, binary md5 ea9b39054f166e94771f838a662712f7); stock v1.1.22 is compile/blueprint only and never a reading source. The movement from the previously pinned rows is NOT compiler-caused. Every row fell by exactly 6 CEK machine steps: the CEK step cost is a constant `mem: 100, cpu: 16000` (`default_machine_cost()` in the fork's `crates/uplc/src/machine/cost_model.rs`), so -600/-96,000 is 6 steps and nothing else. The cause is source, not codegen: `c2237b30` (feat(fault-proofs): complete missing-signature lifecycle) rewrote `onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/field-opening-v1.ak`, adding `resume_opened_field_walk` over the machine-walk resume entry point, which shortens the field-opening path by that fixed step count. Git archaeology confirms no other source this ledger's modules depend on changed after the rows were last pinned. The same per-opening quantum (-300 mem / -48,000 cpu) appears in the canonical-decodability ledger, where a control re-measurement under that ledger's own former rev `2a78108` reproduced the identical shift, establishing the movement as source drift rather than a compiler difference. Both rows remain far inside the GOAL_SPEC 3.3 basis after the re-take (1,857,988 and 1,848,652 mem against a 13,200,000 basis), and no `basisFit` label changed. This ledger derives nothing from its rows, so there is no net to restate.
